evidence.t: Gross revenue at list $5.57M, less deal discounts $170.6k = $5.40M. Refunds $248.4k take it to net revenue of $5.15M.
Ads $753.4k (TCC_RU_PnL; $753k on TCC_Road); TACoS 14.0% (TCC_Road).
Stretch CM4 reads $4.29M on TCC_RU_Year and TCC_IN_7_Rollup, $4,284k on TCC_PP_Plan, $4,285k on TCC_PR_Scenarios and $4.28M on TCC_IN_4_Pricing.

items.observation: The headline "$5.57M revenue" is gross at list, but the TACoS and P&L are on $5.40M. Stretch is rounded three ways.
items.query: Which revenue figure is stored in Target Setting: $5.40M (net of deal discounts), $5.15M (after refunds) or $5.57M (gross at list)?
items.rec: Label $5.57M as gross at list wherever it appears, or lead with $5.40M. Use one stretch figure.
items.next: Joseph updates the labels before the target session. Expected result: the stored revenue matches the P&L it came from.

items.area: How much of the CM4 is borrowed

evidence.t: The family floor on what a rank sells (FAM_CAL, borrowed from Sleephoria) adds +$983.1k. Without it the plan line reads $939.0k against $1.92M.
Without the #1 launch goals (LAUNCH_GOALS=0) CM4 is $1,497k against $1,921k.
Conservative floor: $648.2k over the year (23,804 units).
CL-K6 is shown as decided (keep) on TCC_KC_Calls but as "an open owner question" on TCC_RU_Calls.

items.observation: About half of the $1.92M depends on a borrowed Sleephoria calibration. That is a reasonable starting assumption, but it is not visible next to the headline.
items.query: When will FAM_CAL be replaced by CooLinens' own calibration, and which reading triggers it? Is CL-K6 decided or open?
items.rec: Keep the decisions. Show the sensitivity beside the headline: $1.92M plan, $939k without FAM_CAL, $1.497M without the #1 goals, $648k conservative. Replace FAM_CAL once CooLinens holds its first ranks (light-push read from about Nov 2).
items.next: Joseph adds the sensitivity line and marks CL-K6 consistently. Expected result: targets are approved with the risk in view.

items.area: The ramp from October to December

evidence.t: Plan units: Oct 232 in 13 days, Nov 1,627, Dec 3,564.
That is 17.8 a day in Oct, 54.2 a day in Nov and 115.0 a day in Dec.
Live: 69 units on 16–19 Oct = 17.25 a day with ads; 29 units on 13–15 Oct = 9.7 a day before ads.
November needs 3.1× today's pace and December 6.7×.
Rule R7: two weeks under the conservative line calls a re-plan; re-forecast monthly.

items.observation: October matches the live pace. The November step is large, and nothing on the boards reads actual units against the line every week, so R7 has no data feed.
items.query: What drives the 3× step into November: the pushes, the season (index 0.58 to 0.86) or the deals? Which weekly number should R7 read?
items.rec: Add a weekly read of actual units against the plan line and the conservative line, by size. Our daily recommendation board can report it every Monday.
items.next: PPC adds the weekly line from 27 Oct; Joseph confirms it is the R7 feed. Expected result: a shortfall shows within two weeks, before December stock and budget are committed.

evidence.t: Plan CM4 is below $0 in Oct, Nov, Dec and Jan. The cumulative low is −$88.5k, back above $0 from Feb '27.
Conservative line: low −$216.8k, back above $0 from May '27.
The new order's deposit and balance and the payout timing are not in the model ("5f, Erik's limits").

items.observation: The cash need is not on the boards. CM4 is not cash, and the order deposit lands in the same months as the push spend.
items.query: What is the approved funding limit for Oct–Jan, and will the cash view (5f) be added before targets are stored?
items.rec: Add the cash view before CL-RU3 is decided, with the conservative line as the funding case.
items.next: Erik confirms the limit; Joseph adds 5f. Expected result: the push budget is set within a known cash ceiling.
items.unavailable: Cash flow, order deposit and payout timing are not in the plan files.

items.area: Do listing fixes gate the pushes or price rungs?

evidence.t: CL-L1: "DECIDED · OCT 20 · yes, not a priority". The fixes go in the normal listing queue, not gating the price rungs.
The same board's strategy: "One deadline for the verified defects, by Oct 29 and before any rung".
Rule P5 (Oct 17): "a listing fix precedes any push". The pushes started Oct 19 without the fixes.
Verified defects: the unsourced "VERIFIED 4°F COOLER" tag (CL-L4) and the Queen fitted sheet listed as 60×75 on the size chart (CL-L5).
Each point of refund rate moves CM4 by $55.7k.

items.observation: Three rules on the boards contradict each other. Two of the defects carry risk whatever the priority: an unsourced performance claim, and a size chart error that can cause returns.
items.query: Is CL-L1 final as written, and are the 4°F tag and the size chart exceptions that get fixed now?
items.rec: Edit the boards to match CL-L1. Fix the 4°F tag (remove unless the claims review sources it) and the size chart now, regardless of queue priority.
items.next: Erik / Joseph confirm; the listing team fixes the two items. Expected result: one rule, and no claim or size-chart risk going into December volume.

evidence.t: "From Feb 11" on TCC_Market and TCC_S1. Feb 11 is path L's last rung.
Apr 5 on TCC_PO_Idea and TCC_Road; Apr 8 (rung R8) on TCC_PR_Calendar.
Keeping the deals (CL-DL1, decided) slides the ladder's end to about Aug 26.

items.observation: Three dates are shown for the same price step.
items.query: Which date is the plan of record: Apr 8 (path R) or about Aug 26 (executable calendar with deals)?
items.rec: Show the path R date and the executable date on every board; remove Feb 11.
items.next: Joseph corrects the text. Expected result: the price-tier check against Sleephoria uses the date the price actually lands.

4.5% on TCC_PP_Rules, giving a 38.7% after-refund break-even; TCC_S1 gives 39.1%.
CooLinens has 0 returns so far; its own sales-based read is mature from Jan 18 at the earliest.

items.query: Which rate is used until Jan 18, and who switches to CooLinens' own rate?

items.next: Joseph aligns the boards. Expected result: one break-even line for the profit lanes.
items.unavailable: CooLinens' own return rate (too early: 0 returns so far).

evidence.t: 4.7 stars on 104 ratings, 0% one-star. 205 of 206 written reviews are Vine (Oct 2 – Oct 16).
Vine reviewers under five stars (33): the cool fades 12, slipperiness 9, synthetic feel 7, price 7, pillowcases without zippers 5, colour 4.

items.observation: The rating rests almost entirely on Vine. The top complaint for a cooling product is that the cool fades, and price is already a complaint at $87.99, before the ladder raises it.
items.query: Which of these complaints will the new order or the listing address (CL-PO3 grip and zipper tests), and by when?
items.rec: Read the first organic ratings separately from Vine, and use CL-RR7's triggers on them. Treat "cool fades" as a listing-expectation point (proof, wording) before the price rungs.
items.next: Joseph adds an organic-only rating line; product team answers on CL-PO3. Expected result: an early warning before the rating moves.
